intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a freefall of 8.5 seconds and is a bucket-list adrenaline rush set against stunning Central Otago scenery.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most celebrated Great Walks, traversing alpine meadows, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The 32km trail offers breathtaking views of Harris Saddle and Lake Mackenzie.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing — South Island Equivalent: Mueller Hut Route
experiences.description: Hike the steep Mueller Hut Route from Aoraki/Mount Cook Village up to the iconic red mountain hut perched at 1800m. Enjoy jaw-dropping views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Hooker Valley, and surrounding glaciers. An overnight stay in the hut is an unforgettable experience under the stars.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the majestic fiords of Milford Sound at dawn before the tour boats arrive, then hike the Milford Track section near the sound. Witness towering waterfalls like Stirling Falls up close, spot dolphins and seals, and experience the raw wilderness of Fiordland National Park.

experiences.name: Queenstown Night Food and Wine Trail
experiences.description: Explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene with a guided evening food tour through the town center. Sample Central Otago Pinot Noir, fresh South Island salmon, venison sliders, and artisan cheeses at award-winning restaurants and local eateries along the lakefront and Beach Street precinct.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing — South Island Equivalent: Mueller Hut Route

Enjoy jaw-dropping views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Hooker Valley, and surrounding glaciers. An overnight stay in the hut is an unforgettable experience under the stars.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect baggage, clear customs, and arrange transport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Consider pre-booked airport shuttle or public bus to save money. Check in and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport terminal
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport cafe or a convenience store near the resort upon arrival — budget around NZD $10-15

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival simple. Pre-download offline maps (Maps.me or Google Maps offline) for South Island navigation. Exchange some currency or withdraw NZD from airport ATM. Rest well — big adventures start tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a leisurely wake-up, take a free walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings. Explore the coastline and enjoy the fresh South Island sea air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest town centre (Christchurch or local hub) and visit the free Botanic Gardens or Hagley Park for a relaxed orientation stroll. Pick up a budget grocery run at Pak'nSave or Countdown supermarket to stock snacks and easy meals for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beachfront at the resort. Cook a simple meal using groceries or grab fish and chips from a local takeaway — a classic budget New Zealand dinner.

meals.breakfast: Instant oats or toast from the resort kitchen or nearby dairy — NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Supermarket sandwich or pie from a bakery — NZD $5-8
meals.dinner: Fish and chips from a local takeaway shop — NZD $10-14

day_by_day.notes: This is your orientation and recovery day. Buy a 7-day bus pass or research InterCity bus routes for the days ahead. Download the DOC (Department of Conservation) app for hike info and track conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Early start — catch the InterCity bus or arrange a shuttle toward Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park. The journey from Christchurch area takes approximately 4-5 hours. Enjoy stunning views of Lake Tekapo along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Aoraki/Mount Cook Village. Drop bags at budget accommodation (YHA Mount Cook or DOC campsite). Take the free Kea Point Track (2 hours return) for your first close-up views of the Mueller Glacier and Aoraki/Mount Cook peak.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village for a budget dinner. Stargaze from the village — the Mackenzie Basin is an International Dark Sky Reserve and the views are absolutely free and spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Muesli bars and fruit packed from the supermarket — NZD $3
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the bus — homemade sandwiches or supermarket snacks — NZD $5
meals.dinner: Self-cooked pasta at YHA communal kitchen — NZD $6-8

day_by_day.notes: Book YHA Mount Cook or DOC Campsite in advance — budget beds from NZD $35-45/night. Bring layers; temperatures at Mount Cook can drop significantly even in November. Check DOC website for track conditions before Mueller Hut Route attempt.

day_by_day.morning: Big day — Mueller Hut Route hike begins at sunrise (around 6:00am). The track starts from White Horse Hill Campground. The route is 10km return with 1,000m elevation gain. The first section follows the Sealy Tarns Track with steep metal stairs — challenging but rewarding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Mueller Hut (approximately 3-4 hours ascent). The iconic red mountain hut sits at 1,800m with jaw-dropping panoramic views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Mueller Glacier, and surrounding peaks. Enjoy your packed lunch with one of the best views in New Zealand. Begin descent carefully.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village by late afternoon. Soak tired legs, shower, and cook a hearty dinner at the YHA kitchen. Share stories with fellow hikers and get tips for upcoming days.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and banana before the hike — NZD $3
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Mueller Hut — energy bars, trail mix, cheese and crackers — NZD $6
meals.dinner: Self-cooked rice and lentil curry at YHA kitchen — NZD $7-9

day_by_day.notes: Mueller Hut Route is graded as Intermediate-Advanced. Wear proper hiking boots, carry 2+ litres of water, sunscreen, and layers. November snow on upper sections is possible — check conditions with DOC the evening before. This is the South Island equivalent of the Tongariro Alpine Crossing experience.

day_by_day.morning: Rest your legs with the easier Hooker Valley Track (10km return, flat). Walk past swing bridges with stunning reflections of Aoraki/Mount Cook in Hooker Lake — one of New Zealand's most iconic and completely free walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catch an afternoon shuttle or InterCity bus toward Queenstown (approximately 4 hours). Arrive in Queenstown by early evening and check into a budget hostel (Base Queenstown, Haka Lodge, or Nomads Queenstown — from NZD $30-40/night).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Queenstown waterfront on Lake Wakatipu for free. Browse the lively Queenstown town centre and grab a budget dinner.

meals.breakfast: Toast and peanut butter at YHA — NZD $2
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on the bus — NZD $4
meals.dinner: Fergburger is iconic but pricey — opt for a supermarket meal deal or Pak'nSave dinner — NZD $8-12

day_by_day.notes: Book your Queenstown hostel in advance — November is shoulder season but Queenstown fills up fast. Research bungee jumping deals tonight — AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy is the world's first commercial bungee site and prices start around NZD $165-200. Look for online discount codes.

day_by_day.morning: BUNGEE JUMPING DAY! Head to AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy (43m drop over the turquoise Kawarau River) — the world's first commercial bungee jumping site, approximately 23km from Queenstown. Book the earliest slot to beat crowds. This is a bucket-list experience!
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, recover with a walk across the historic Kawarau Bridge and enjoy the scenic gorge area for free. Return to Queenstown and explore the free Queenstown Gardens on the lakefront peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungee jump at a hostel bar or grab happy hour deals at one of Queenstown's bars. Many hostels offer free or cheap social events in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Hostel free breakfast (if included) or toast at the hostel kitchen — NZD $2-4
meals.lunch: Supermarket sandwich near Kawarau Bridge or packed lunch — NZD $5-7
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market (if running on Fridays) — great budget street food options from NZD $8-12

day_by_day.notes: AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy costs approximately NZD $165-200. Book online in advance for best price. Video/photo packages are extra — decide in advance if worth the splurge. Wear comfortable clothing without loose items. The experience includes shuttle from Queenstown town centre.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Ben Lomond Track from Queenstown (via gondola base or full walk up). The summit track is 11km return with 1,400m elevation gain and offers 360-degree views of Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and Cecil Peak. Start early — allow 5-7 hours for the full summit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the descent or turn back at Saddle (1,326m) if time or energy is limited — still spectacular views. The track is free and accessible directly from town.
day_by_day.evening: Recover at the hostel. Visit the free Queenstown waterfront sunset — golden hour over Lake Wakatipu with The Remarkables in the background is unforgettable. Cook dinner at the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Oats and banana before the hike — NZD $3
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — crackers, cheese, dried fruit — NZD $5
meals.dinner: Self-cooked pasta bolognese at hostel kitchen — NZD $6-8

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond Track is rated Advanced. Conditions in November can be unpredictable — carry extra layers, rain jacket, and plenty of water. The gondola (NZD $45 return) can be taken to skip the lower forest section if budget allows, but walking the full track is free and rewarding.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free walk along the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (3.5 hours return) for panoramic views over the town and lake. A quieter alternative to Ben Lomond with beautiful native bush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catch an InterCity bus or Naked Bus to Te Anau (approximately 2.5 hours, from NZD $20-35). Te Anau is the gateway to Fiordland National Park. Check into budget accommodation (Te Anau YHA or Barnyard Backpackers — from NZD $30-38/night).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Te Anau lakefront at sunset — Lake Te Anau is New Zealand's second-largest lake and the views are stunning and free. Plan tomorrow's Fiordland adventure.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen breakfast — toast and eggs — NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Bus snacks packed from Queenstown supermarket — NZD $4
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal at Te Anau hostel or a cheap pub meal — NZD $10-15

day_by_day.notes: Book Milford Sound day trip in advance if budget allows (from NZD $75-100 for bus + cruise combo). Alternatively, the Milford Sound Highway drive itself (if you can arrange a car share or hitchhike) offers world-class free scenery. Check DOC for free day walks in Fiordland.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early on the Milford Sound day trip bus from Te Anau (departs ~8:00am). The 2-hour drive through Fiordland National Park along the Milford Road passes Mirror Lakes, The Chasm, and the Homer Tunnel — all free stops with incredible scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Milford Sound and board a budget scenic cruise (Real Journeys or Go Orange — from NZD $45-75). Cruise past Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, Bowen Falls, and spot seals, dolphins, and penguins if lucky. Return bus to Te Anau arrives by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Te Anau hostel. Cook dinner and review photos from the day. The Milford Sound experience is genuinely one of the world's great natural wonders.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast before bus departure — NZD $3
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the cruise (bring your own to avoid expensive onboard prices) — NZD $6-8
meals.dinner: Self-cooked dinner at hostel — rice and vegetables — NZD $6

day_by_day.notes: Budget for the full Milford Sound day: bus (~NZD $30-40 return from Te Anau) + cruise (~NZD $45-75) = NZD $75-115 total. This is worth every cent for a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Book in advance online for best prices. Bring a rain jacket — Milford receives over 7,000mm of rain per year.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Kepler Track Day Walk from Te Anau — take the free shuttle or walk to the Control Gates and follow the lakeside section of this Great Walk for as long as time allows. The beech forest and lake views are stunning without needing a Great Walk pass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Te Anau and catch an afternoon bus back toward the east coast. Head to Dunedin via Invercargill (InterCity bus, approximately 4-5 hours total, from NZD $25-45). Check into Dunedin hostel (Hogwartz or On Top Backpackers — from NZD $28-38/night).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Dunedin's vibrant student city centre on foot. The Octagon (city centre) is lively and free to explore. Browse street art and Victorian-era architecture.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen — oats and fruit — NZD $3
meals.lunch: Supermarket lunch in Te Anau before bus — NZD $5-7
meals.dinner: Dunedin has great budget food — try a student-area cafe or supermarket meal — NZD $8-12

day_by_day.notes: Dunedin is New Zealand's student city and very budget-friendly. Look for cheap eats near the University of Otago campus. The city has free museums, galleries, and incredible wildlife nearby at Otago Peninsula.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the free Otago Museum (natural history and science exhibits) in Dunedin city centre. Then walk up Baldwin Street — the world's steepest residential street — for a fun free activity and great views over the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a free or cheap bus to Otago Peninsula (approximately 30 minutes). Walk the free Sandfly Bay Track (1.5 hours return) to see wild New Zealand sea lions on the beach — a truly remarkable free wildlife encounter. Check if yellow-eyed penguins are visible at dusk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Dunedin city. Grab dinner in the student quarter — many cafes and restaurants offer great value. Explore the lively bar scene if interested (many student bars have cheap drinks).

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen — toast and peanut butter — NZD $2-3
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Sandfly Bay — NZD $4-5
meals.dinner: Student area restaurant or supermarket meal — NZD $8-12

day_by_day.notes: Otago Peninsula wildlife is free and world-class. Sea lions at Sandfly Bay are wild and unpredictable — keep your distance (at least 20m). Yellow-eyed penguin viewing is best at dusk. Some private penguin hides charge NZD $30-50 but DOC areas are free.

day_by_day.morning: Catch an early bus or arrange transport back toward Christchurch (approximately 5-6 hours by InterCity, from NZD $30-50). The coastal route passes through Moeraki — stop to see the famous Moeraki Boulders on the beach (free access from the beach, or NZD $2 via cafe path).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Christchurch and check into a budget hostel (Jailhouse Accommodation or Dorset House — from NZD $28-40/night). Visit the free Christchurch Botanic Gardens and walk along the Avon River Precinct.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Christchurch Arts Centre and Cathedral Square area. Visit the free Canterbury Museum before closing time (usually 5pm). Grab dinner in the revitalized city centre.

meals.breakfast: Early hostel kitchen breakfast in Dunedin — NZD $3
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the bus or Moeraki village cafe pie — NZD $5-8
meals.dinner: Christchurch food court or supermarket meal — NZD $8-12

day_by_day.notes: The Moeraki Boulders are a must-stop — these spherical geological formations on the beach are extraordinary. Access from the beach is free. The bus may stop briefly — confirm with InterCity when booking. Christchurch has excellent free cultural attractions rebuilt after the 2011 earthquake.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in New Zealand! Visit the free Christchurch Art Gallery (Te Puna o Waiwhetū) — one of New Zealand's finest contemporary art galleries. Then walk through the Transitional Cathedral (Cardboard Cathedral) — a remarkable piece of post-earthquake architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Christchurch Arts Centre markets or cheap souvenir shops. Pick up New Zealand-made goods at budget prices. Pack bags and prepare for departure. Head to Christchurch Airport via the Christchurch Metro bus (NZD $3.50) or airport shuttle.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Christchurch Airport. Reflect on an incredible 13-day South Island adventure — Mueller Hut Route, Kawarau Bungee, Milford Sound, Otago Peninsula wildlife, and so much more!

meals.breakfast: Final hostel kitchen breakfast — NZD $3-5
meals.lunch: Christchurch city cafe or supermarket — NZD $7-10
meals.dinner: Airport terminal meal or pack snacks for the flight — NZD $10-15

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Christchurch Airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Spend any remaining NZD cash on snacks or last-minute gifts. Declare any food items at customs. Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights and accommodation already booked): NZD $800-1,100 covering transport, food, activities, and entrance fees.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch or Queenstown Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront accommodation. Check in and settle into your room. Light refreshments if available at the resort.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport snack
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack from the airport or a late-night convenience option near the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30 so no sightseeing is planned. Confirm transfer arrangements in advance. Keep Day 2 morning relaxed to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow walk along the beachfront to orient yourself and breathe in the South Island air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area around your resort. Visit a nearby scenic lookout or coastal walk. If near Queenstown, stroll along the Queenstown Bay waterfront and browse the town center shops and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown Night Food and Wine Trail — Join a guided evening food tour through Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene, sampling local wines, craft beers, and regional New Zealand dishes across multiple stops in the town center.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or café on-site
meals.lunch: Fergburger, Queenstown — iconic mid-range burger joint beloved by locals and visitors alike
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Queenstown Night Food and Wine Trail tasting experience

day_by_day.notes: The food trail is an ideal gentle introduction to Queenstown without physical exertion after a long-haul flight. Book the food trail in advance as spots fill quickly in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a shuttle to Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park (approximately 4 hours from Queenstown). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Mackenzie Basin and turquoise Lake Pukaki.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Mueller Hut Route hike from Aoraki/Mount Cook Village. The trail climbs steeply through alpine terrain with stunning views of the Hooker Valley and surrounding glaciers. Hike to Sealy Tarns as a partial option if the full route is too demanding.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mount Cook Village. Relax with dinner at a local restaurant. If staying overnight near Mount Cook, enjoy the internationally recognized Aoraki Dark Sky Reserve for stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Pack a takeaway breakfast from the resort or grab a bite at a café in Twizel en route
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a Queenstown supermarket or Twizel deli — eat on the trail
meals.dinner: Old Mountaineers Café & Bar, Mount Cook Village — mid-range, hearty meals with mountain views

day_by_day.notes: The Mueller Hut Route is a full-day commitment. Start early and check weather conditions before departing. Wear sturdy hiking boots and carry extra layers — alpine weather can change rapidly even in November.

day_by_day.morning: If you stayed near Mount Cook overnight, complete the Hooker Valley Track — an easy 3-hour return walk through glacial moraines to the Hooker Glacier terminal lake with iconic Aoraki views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Queenstown via Lake Tekapo. Stop at the Church of the Good Shepherd and enjoy a swim or walk around the turquoise lake shores. Explore Tekapo township.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Rest and recharge. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Café by the Lake, Lake Tekapo — popular mid-range café with lake views
meals.lunch: Mackenzie's Bar & Grill, Lake Tekapo — casual mid-range dining
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or a nearby local restaurant in Queenstown

day_by_day.notes: This is a scenic transition day combining easy hiking with a beautiful drive. Lake Tekapo is stunning in November when lupins may be in bloom along the shoreline.

day_by_day.morning: Prepare for the Nevis Bungy Jump — the highlight adventure day. Transfer to the Nevis Bungy platform via the AJ Hackett shuttle from Queenstown. Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-bungy adrenaline wind-down. Return to Queenstown. Browse the waterfront, visit the Queenstown Gardens, or take the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak for panoramic views of the Remarkables and Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Queenstown to mark the bungy achievement. Explore the lively Queenstown bar scene if desired.

meals.breakfast: Vudu Café & Larder, Queenstown — excellent coffee and wholesome breakfast before the big jump
meals.lunch: The Bunker Restaurant, Queenstown — cozy mid-range bistro with great burgers and wraps
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant, Queenstown — mid-to-upper mid-range, locally sourced New Zealand cuisine by chef Josh Emmett

day_by_day.notes: Book the Nevis Bungy well in advance through AJ Hackett. Minimum weight requirements apply. Avoid heavy meals before the jump. The jump experience includes a scenic cable car ride to the platform suspended above the gorge.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the adrenaline of Day 5. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort. Optional: gentle yoga or a swim if resort facilities allow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic cruise on Lake Wakatipu — the TSS Earnslaw vintage steamship offers a 1.5-hour cruise with views of the surrounding mountains and a visit to Walter Peak High Country Farm.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Arrowtown, a charming gold-rush era village 20 minutes from Queenstown. Walk the historic main street, visit the Chinese Settlement ruins, and enjoy dinner in this quaint township.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local café near the accommodation
meals.lunch: On-board the TSS Earnslaw or at Walter Peak Farm café
meals.dinner: Provisions of Arrowtown — highly regarded mid-range restaurant with seasonal New Zealand produce

day_by_day.notes: The TSS Earnslaw cruise is a relaxing and iconic Queenstown experience. Book tickets online in advance. Arrowtown is particularly beautiful in November with spring foliage.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Te Anau (approximately 2 hours from Queenstown). This is the gateway town to Fiordland National Park. Check in or drop bags at accommodation. Walk the Te Anau lakefront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves — a boat trip across Lake Te Anau followed by a guided cave tour through ancient limestone caverns lit by thousands of glowworms.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Te Anau. Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant and prepare gear for the Routeburn Track starting the next morning.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast or stop at a café in Kingston en route
meals.lunch: Miles Better Pies, Te Anau — beloved local bakery with hearty pies and pastries
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant, Te Anau — mid-range, cozy restaurant in a historic cottage with New Zealand game and seafood

day_by_day.notes: Book the Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour through Real Journeys in advance. Te Anau is the last major town before Fiordland — stock up on trail snacks and supplies for the Routeburn Track.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer to the Routeburn Track trailhead (Routeburn Shelter, approximately 1 hour from Te Anau via Glenorchy). Begin hiking the Routeburn Track — one of New Zealand's Great Walks. Morning section covers the Routeburn Flats through ancient beech forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the track to Routeburn Falls Hut. Admire the spectacular Routeburn Falls and the transition into alpine terrain above the bush line. Arrive at the hut for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Routeburn Falls Hut (DOC Great Walk hut). Enjoy the alpine sunset views, meet fellow trampers, and rest up for the next day's alpine crossing.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Te Anau accommodation before transfer
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — sandwiches, energy bars, fruit
meals.dinner: Self-prepared meal at the hut using packed supplies — pasta, instant meals, or dehydrated hiking food

day_by_day.notes: Routeburn Track hut passes must be booked in advance through DOC (Department of Conservation). November is peak season — book months ahead. Carry all food, a sleeping bag liner, and wet weather gear.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Routeburn Falls Hut. Hike through the spectacular alpine section of the Routeburn Track — crossing Lake Harris saddle with panoramic views of the Harris Mountains and the Darran Mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Lake Mackenzie Hut. Enjoy a swim in the crystal-clear alpine lake if weather permits. Rest and take in the stunning glacially carved valley scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Lake Mackenzie Hut. Relax, journal, and enjoy the remote Fiordland atmosphere under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at Routeburn Falls Hut
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch eaten at Harris Saddle or en route
meals.dinner: Self-prepared hut meal — dehydrated meals, instant noodles, or packed supplies

day_by_day.notes: The Harris Saddle section is exposed to alpine weather — carry waterproofs and warm layers regardless of forecast. The views from the saddle on a clear day are among the finest in New Zealand.

day_by_day.morning: Final section of the Routeburn Track from Lake Mackenzie Hut to the Divide (Hollyford end). Hike through the Orchard and Earland Falls section — a beautiful descent through moss-draped beech forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach The Divide trailhead. Board the shuttle back toward Te Anau or Queenstown. Decompress and celebrate completing the Routeburn Great Walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown or Te Anau. Hot shower, comfortable bed, and a well-earned restaurant dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at Lake Mackenzie Hut
meals.lunch: Final trail lunch at Earland Falls or The Divide
meals.dinner: Ristorante Pizzeria Paradiso, Queenstown — beloved mid-range Italian restaurant, perfect post-hike comfort food

day_by_day.notes: Arrange shuttle pickup from The Divide in advance through Tracknet or Topline Tours. The Divide is about 90 minutes from Te Anau. Celebrate completing one of New Zealand's finest Great Walks.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Milford Sound (approximately 4 hours via Te Anau). Depart early to enjoy the stunning Milford Road — stop at Mirror Lakes, the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain, and Homer Tunnel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo — Paddle through the majestic fiords at a quieter afternoon time, experiencing Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, and Bowen Falls up close by kayak, followed by a short guided hike in the surrounding rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Te Anau or overnight in the Milford Sound Lodge if budget allows. Enjoy dinner with views of the fiord.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Queenstown or Te Anau before the drive
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten en route at Mirror Lakes or a scenic stop
meals.dinner: Milford Sound Lodge dining room or, if returning to Te Anau, The Sandfly Café — casual mid-range lakeside dining

day_by_day.notes: Depart Queenstown no later than 6:00am to reach Milford Sound in time for the afternoon kayak. Book the kayak and hike combo in advance through Rosco's Milford Kayaks or similar operator. Sandflies are intense at Milford — bring strong insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Queenstown from Te Anau or Milford. Stop at Lake Marian for a short optional hike (2 hours return) — a hidden gem in the Hollyford Valley with a stunning alpine lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Back in Queenstown, enjoy a wine tasting experience in the Gibbston Valley — New Zealand's highest wine-producing region, just 20 minutes from Queenstown. Visit Gibbston Valley Winery or Peregrine Wines for a cellar door tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Queenstown. Stroll the waterfront, pick up souvenirs, and enjoy a special farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café in Te Anau or packed breakfast on the road
meals.lunch: Gibbston Valley Winery restaurant — mid-range, excellent local produce and wine pairings
meals.dinner: Fishbone Bar & Grill, Queenstown — mid-range seafood and New Zealand classics with waterfront atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The Gibbston Valley is stunning in late spring/early summer. Book the winery tour or tasting in advance. This is a great opportunity to purchase a bottle of Central Otago Pinot Noir as a souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in New Zealand. Enjoy a last breakfast at the resort with beachfront views. Pack, check out, and take a final walk along the waterfront or visit a local café for coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — visit the Queenstown i-SITE for any last-minute souvenirs, or take a short walk in the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2 hours return) for a final panoramic farewell view of the lake and mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Queenstown Airport for departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days of hiking, bungy jumping, kayaking, and exploring the spectacular South Island of New Zealand.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or Vudu Café & Larder for a memorable last coffee and meal
meals.lunch: Fergburger, Queenstown — end the trip with a classic Queenstown tradition
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for Queenstown Airport check-in and security. Queenstown Airport is small but can be busy in peak season. Confirm your departure flight details and arrange airport transfer in advance.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a freefall of 8.5 seconds and is a bucket-list adrenaline rush set against stunning Central Otago scenery.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most celebrated Great Walks, traversing alpine meadows, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The 32km trail offers breathtaking views of Harris Saddle and Lake Mackenzie.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing — South Island Equivalent: Mueller Hut Route
experiences.description: Hike the steep Mueller Hut Route from Aoraki/Mount Cook Village up to the iconic red mountain hut perched at 1800m. Enjoy jaw-dropping views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Hooker Valley, and surrounding glaciers. An overnight stay in the hut is an unforgettable experience under the stars.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the majestic fiords of Milford Sound at dawn before the tour boats arrive, then hike the Milford Track section near the sound. Witness towering waterfalls like Stirling Falls up close, spot dolphins and seals, and experience the raw wilderness of Fiordland National Park.

experiences.name: Queenstown Night Food and Wine Trail
experiences.description: Explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene with a guided evening food tour through the town center. Sample Central Otago Pinot Noir, fresh South Island salmon, venison sliders, and artisan cheeses at award-winning restaurants and local eateries along the lakefront and Beach Street precinct.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer from Queenstown Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome amenity (chilled champagne and local cheese board prepared by the resort), and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light in-room dining from the resort's late-night menu — recommended: smoked salmon blinis, New Zealand green-lipped mussel chowder, and a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with the resort concierge before travel. Request early luggage delivery to room to minimize disruption. Keep the first night simple and restorative — big adventures begin tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort breakfast to recover from travel. Afterward, take a private guided orientation walk along the beachfront and surrounding resort grounds to acclimate to the South Island scenery. Meet with the concierge to confirm upcoming bookings and gear requirements.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic helicopter flight over the Queenstown basin and Remarkables mountain range — a premium introductory perspective of the South Island landscape. Land at a private high-country station for a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort chef.
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown Night Food and Wine Trail — explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene with a guided evening food tour through the town center, sampling craft wines, artisan cheeses, venison sliders, and locally sourced small plates at curated stops.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet and à la carte at the Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — eggs Benedict with Marlborough smoked salmon, fresh fruit, and flat whites
meals.lunch: Private gourmet high-country picnic — charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh bread, and Central Otago Pinot Gris
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Queenstown Night Food and Wine Trail experience — multiple tasting stops through town

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter scenic flight through the resort concierge. The Night Food and Wine Trail typically departs around 6:00 PM from central Queenstown — arrange private return transfer to resort afterward.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning preparation and briefing for the Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. Private luxury coach transfer to the Nevis site. Complete the iconic leap and optional second jump for the ultimate adrenaline experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-jump recovery and celebration at a private riverside lounge near the Nevis site. Return to Queenstown and enjoy a restorative spa treatment at the Aegean Bliss Resort — deep tissue massage or hot stone therapy recommended after the physical exhilaration of the morning.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Queenstown's finest fine-dining restaurant — Amisfield Winery & Bistro or Rata (by Josh Emett) — featuring locally sourced South Island produce, game meats, and an exceptional Central Otago wine list.

meals.breakfast: Light, high-protein resort breakfast before the jump — avocado toast, poached eggs, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet grazing platter and sparkling wine at the Nevis riverside celebration lounge (arrange with AJ Hackett premium package)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant, Queenstown — tasting menu with wine pairing featuring Central Otago Pinot Noir and Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy requires a minimum weight of 45kg and has a maximum of 127kg. Wear comfortable, fitted clothing. Purchase the premium video and photo package to capture the jump. Spa must be booked in advance through the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private charter vehicle toward Glenorchy and the start of the Routeburn Track Great Walk. Begin hiking the first section of this celebrated trail — traversing ancient beech forest, crossing crystal-clear mountain streams, and ascending toward the alpine meadows above the tree line.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Routeburn Track to the Routeburn Falls Hut area, taking in the dramatic waterfall and sweeping valley views. Enjoy a gourmet packed lunch prepared by the resort in this spectacular alpine setting before returning on the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown by private vehicle. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort's signature beachfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — hearty oatmeal, eggs, whole grain toast, and energy-boosting smoothies to fuel the hike
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch provided by the resort — artisan sandwiches, energy bars, fruit, and a thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront restaurant — pan-seared South Island blue cod, roasted kumara, and a glass of Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track day hike covers approximately 16–20 km return to Routeburn Falls — moderate to strenuous difficulty. Wear layered hiking clothing and waterproof boots. Weather on the track can change rapidly — pack a rain shell. This is a day hike version; the full Great Walk multi-day option is available later in the itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery morning — gentle yoga session on the resort's beachfront deck at sunrise, followed by a swim in the resort's infinity pool overlooking the water. Visit the resort's wellness spa for a rejuvenating facial or hydrotherapy treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private wine tour of the Central Otago wine region — one of the world's southernmost wine-producing areas, famous for Pinot Noir. Visit two to three boutique wineries (Amisfield, Peregrine, or Valli Vineyard) with private tastings and a winery lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard a private charter vessel — champagne, canapés, and panoramic views of the Remarkables and Cecil Peak as the sun sets over the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Poolside resort breakfast — açaí bowls, smashed avocado, cold-pressed juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Private winery lunch at Amisfield Winery — seasonal tasting menu paired with estate wines in their iconic stone bistro
meals.dinner: Canapés and champagne aboard the private Lake Wakatipu sunset cruise, followed by a light resort supper on return

day_by_day.notes: Book the private wine tour and lake cruise through the resort concierge well in advance. November is spring in New Zealand — evenings on the lake can be cool, so bring a light jacket for the cruise.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day adventure: depart early by private luxury coach to Te Anau — the gateway to Fiordland National Park. Arrive and check into a premium lakeside lodge for a two-night Fiordland base. Explore Te Anau township and the tranquil Te Anau lakefront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Te Anau Glowworm Caves private tour — a magical boat journey across Lake Te Anau into the ancient limestone caves, where thousands of glowworms illuminate the underground chambers in a breathtaking natural light show.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium Te Anau restaurant — Redcliff Restaurant is renowned for its South Island game meats, including venison, wild boar, and fresh Fiordland crayfish, in a charming heritage cottage setting.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast at Aegean Bliss before departure — eggs Florentine, fresh pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch en route to Te Anau, enjoyed at a scenic lakeside stop along the way
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant, Te Anau — Fiordland crayfish thermidor, slow-braised venison, and a Marlborough Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Queenstown to Te Anau is approximately 2 hours. Arrange private luxury coach or self-drive rental. Book the Glowworm Caves private tour in advance as it is extremely popular. Pack hiking layers for the next two days in Fiordland.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau at dawn for the 90-minute scenic drive to Milford Sound along the iconic Milford Road. Arrive early to begin the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo — paddle through the majestic fiords at dawn before the tour boats arrive, experiencing the mirror-still waters, towering cliffs, and cascading waterfalls in near-total solitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, embark on the hiking component of the combo — trail through the Fiordland rainforest along the Milford foreshore, spotting native wildlife including Fiordland crested penguins, fur seals, and kea parrots. Enjoy a gourmet packed lunch at a scenic waterfall viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau by private vehicle. Celebrate the day with a premium dinner at the lakeside lodge restaurant, featuring Fiordland whitebait fritters and fresh blue cod.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-dawn breakfast at the Te Anau lodge — high-energy porridge, eggs, and strong coffee before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch at Milford Sound — smoked salmon wraps, fresh fruit, chocolate, and a thermos of hot tea
meals.dinner: Te Anau lakeside lodge restaurant — Fiordland whitebait fritters, pan-roasted blue cod, and a Waipara Valley Chardonnay

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound weather is highly unpredictable — Fiordland receives over 7 meters of rainfall annually, and rain actually enhances the experience by creating hundreds of temporary waterfalls. Wear full waterproof gear regardless of forecast. The kayak and hike combo is a full-day experience of approximately 8–9 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Te Anau — optional guided walk along the Te Anau lakefront or a peaceful kayak on the calm lake waters. Visit the Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre to learn about the ecology and geology of this UNESCO World Heritage area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Te Anau and travel north toward Lake Tekapo via the scenic Mackenzie Basin. Stop at the Church of the Good Shepherd and the famous lupine-lined shores of Lake Tekapo (November is peak lupin season — fields of purple and pink blooms frame the turquoise glacial lake).
day_by_day.evening: Check into a premium lakeside property at Lake Tekapo. Dinner at Mackenzie's Restaurant at the Peppers Bluewater Resort — renowned for its alpine views and South Island lamb dishes. Afterward, experience the Lake Tekapo Dark Sky Reserve Stargazing tour — one of the world's best stargazing locations.

meals.breakfast: Te Anau lodge breakfast — continental spread, fresh eggs, and coffee before checkout
meals.lunch: Scenic roadside lunch stop at a Mackenzie Basin café — venison pie, flat white, and fresh baking
meals.dinner: Mackenzie's Restaurant, Lake Tekapo — slow-roasted South Island lamb rack, roasted root vegetables, and a Central Otago Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Te Anau to Lake Tekapo is approximately 4.5 hours — plan for scenic stops. November lupins at Lake Tekapo are world-famous; bring a camera. Book the Dark Sky Reserve stargazing tour in advance through the Earth & Sky Observatory — clear nights offer views of the Milky Way in extraordinary detail.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise photography walk along the Lake Tekapo shoreline among the lupins. After breakfast, depart for Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park — a 1-hour scenic drive through the Mackenzie Basin with increasingly dramatic alpine views. Check into The Hermitage Hotel, the iconic luxury lodge at the foot of New Zealand's highest peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Mueller Hut Route — hike the steep, rewarding trail from Aoraki/Mount Cook Village up through the Sealy Tarns to the iconic red Mueller Hut perched high above the Hooker Valley. The views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Hooker Glacier, and the surrounding Southern Alps are among the finest in New Zealand.
day_by_day.evening: Descend and return to The Hermitage. Enjoy a well-earned dinner at The Hermitage's fine-dining restaurant, The Alpine Restaurant, with floor-to-ceiling views of Aoraki/Mount Cook illuminated by the setting sun.

meals.breakfast: Lake Tekapo lodge breakfast — eggs Benedict, fresh fruit salad, and specialty coffee before departure
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch from The Hermitage enjoyed at the Sealy Tarns viewpoint on the Mueller Hut Route
meals.dinner: The Alpine Restaurant, The Hermitage — Canterbury lamb, local salmon, and a premium South Island wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The Mueller Hut Route is a strenuous 10km round trip with 1,030m of elevation gain — allow 6–8 hours. Wear sturdy hiking boots and carry layered clothing, as conditions near the hut can be alpine even in November. The hut itself is a New Zealand icon — if weather permits, consider staying overnight (book DOC hut pass in advance) for a sunrise experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Hooker Valley Track walk — a relatively gentle 3-hour return hike through the Hooker Valley with three swing bridges, glacial lakes with icebergs, and unobstructed views of Aoraki/Mount Cook. One of the most scenic and accessible walks in New Zealand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic glacier flight — board a ski-plane or helicopter for a breathtaking aerial tour of the Aoraki/Mount Cook and Southern Alps glacier system, including a snow landing on the Tasman Glacier — the longest glacier in New Zealand. A truly once-in-a-lifetime alpine experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown via private charter or scenic flight. Check back into the Aegean Bliss Resort. Celebrate the midpoint of the trip with a premium dinner at Botswana Butchery or Fishbone Bar & Grill in Queenstown.

meals.breakfast: Early Hermitage breakfast — full cooked breakfast with views of Aoraki/Mount Cook at sunrise
meals.lunch: Hermitage packed lunch enjoyed at the Hooker Valley Terminal Lake viewpoint
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery, Queenstown — prime South Island beef tenderloin, truffle fries, and a Hawke's Bay Syrah

day_by_day.notes: Glacier flights from Mount Cook are weather-dependent and can be cancelled or rescheduled on short notice — have a flexible backup plan. Book the scenic flight with Mount Cook Ski Planes & Helicopters in advance. The snow landing experience is an upgrade worth booking.

day_by_day.morning: Multi-day Routeburn Track Great Walk — Day 1. Depart Queenstown early by private shuttle to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead at Glenorchy. Begin the full Great Walk, hiking through pristine beech forest and alongside the Routeburn River to Routeburn Flats Hut (11.4 km). Check into the premium guided lodge accommodation (Routeburn Track guided walk with Ultimate Hikes recommended for luxury experience).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking from Routeburn Flats up to Routeburn Falls Hut (2.5 km further, 240m ascent) — passing the spectacular Routeburn Falls. Settle into the hut, explore the alpine surroundings, and enjoy the dramatic mountain panoramas.
day_by_day.evening: Communal guided lodge dinner at Routeburn Falls Lodge (Ultimate Hikes guided walk includes catered meals) — a warm, hearty three-course dinner in the mountains, swapping stories with fellow hikers under a sky full of Southern Hemisphere stars.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before shuttle departure — high-energy hiking fuel
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet trail lunch enjoyed at the Routeburn Flats alongside the river
meals.dinner: Catered three-course dinner at Routeburn Falls Lodge — hearty mountain cuisine with wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ultimate Hikes guided Routeburn Track experience well in advance — this premium guided version includes catered lodge accommodation, making it far superior to the independent DOC hut experience. The guided walk is 3 days/2 nights. Carry only a daypack — Ultimate Hikes provides a gear transfer service.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Great Walk — Day 2. Depart Routeburn Falls Hut and ascend to the alpine zone above the tree line, crossing the iconic Harris Saddle at 1,255m with 360-degree views across Fiordland and the Darran Mountains. This is the most dramatic section of the entire track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Harris Saddle through the spectacular Lake Harris basin and along the Hollyford Valley to Lake Mackenzie Lodge (11.1 km for the day). Arrive at the beautifully situated lodge overlooking the pristine alpine lake. Rest, freshen up, and explore the lake surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views over Lake Mackenzie from the lodge deck with a glass of New Zealand wine. Catered lodge dinner — a celebration of the day's extraordinary alpine hiking achievement.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast at Routeburn Falls — porridge, eggs, toast, and coffee before the big day's hike
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch enjoyed at Harris Saddle — the roof of the Routeburn Track with panoramic views
meals.dinner: Catered three-course dinner at Lake Mackenzie Lodge — New Zealand lamb, roasted vegetables, and a Marlborough Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: The Harris Saddle section is exposed to alpine weather — carry full waterproofs and warm layers regardless of morning conditions. The optional side trip to Conical Hill from Harris Saddle adds 1 hour but delivers arguably the finest views on the entire South Island. Highly recommended if weather is clear.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Great Walk — Day 3 (Final Day). Depart Lake Mackenzie Lodge and hike the final section of the Routeburn Track through ancient podocarp forest to the Divide car park on the Milford Road (8.2 km). This final section descends through lush rainforest with beautiful river crossings and valley views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private shuttle transfer from The Divide back to Queenstown (approximately 2 hours). Return to Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a luxurious long soak in the resort spa bath, a deep tissue massage, and time to relax and reflect on an extraordinary 13-day South Island adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at Queenstown's most prestigious restaurant — Amisfield Winery Bistro or a private chef's table experience arranged through the resort — celebrating the completion of an epic New Zealand South Island journey with the finest local produce, wines, and company.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast at Lake Mackenzie — a satisfying send-off before the last day of hiking
meals.lunch: Celebratory lunch at a Queenstown waterfront restaurant on return — Fishbone Bar & Grill for fresh Fiordland crayfish and chilled Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc
meals.dinner: Private chef's table farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort or Amisfield Winery Bistro — full tasting menu with paired Central Otago wines, celebrating the end of an extraordinary South Island adventure

day_by_day.notes: Arrange resort spa treatments and farewell dinner reservations in advance through the concierge. If departing New Zealand the following day, confirm airport transfer and any onward travel logistics this evening. Consider purchasing Central Otago Pinot Noir and Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc from a local bottle shop to take home as souvenirs of the trip.
